questions.q: Why were mass schools introduced, according to Robinson?
a: To produce standardized workers for factory jobs
To teach children art and music
To raise the general level of public health
To prepare every student for university
questions.why: Lesson 1 ties mass education to the industrial revolution, which needed standardized knowledge and obedience.

questions.q: What does the gardener metaphor mean for teaching?
a: You cannot force growth but can feed a natural desire to learn
You must prune away every bad habit as early as possible
You should plant the same crop in every child
You have to water on a strict fixed schedule
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a gardener cannot make plants grow, but can nurture the curiosity already inside them.

questions.q: How does Robinson suggest teachers spark curiosity?
a: By connecting lessons to students' own interests
By testing students more frequently
By lecturing for longer periods
By keeping lessons strictly academic
questions.why: The summary gives examples like linking math to baseball, history to the local city and music to students' own genres.

questions.q: Which three competencies does Robinson say children need most?
a: Curiosity, creativity and criticism
Reading, writing and arithmetic
Discipline, obedience and memory
Confidence, competition and leadership
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that facts and hard skills fade in value, while these three attitudes remain timeless.

questions.q: What does criticism mean in this context?
a: Questioning answers and telling fact from opinion
Pointing out other people's mistakes
Rejecting every idea you hear
Judging art and literature formally
questions.why: The summary defines criticism as the courage to question even your own answers and separate signal from noise.
